QF.id: Retirement Planning Products: Other Investment Products_24

question.text: An immediate annuity differs from a deferred annuity in that:

answer.text: An immediate annuity starts paying income right away while a deferred annuity starts at a future date
An immediate annuity has higher returns than a deferred annuity
A deferred annuity pays more frequently than an immediate annuity
An immediate annuity requires lower investment than a deferred annuity

explanation.text: The Logic: An immediate annuity begins paying income immediately after purchase, while a deferred annuity builds the corpus during the deferment period and uses it to buy the annuity at the vesting age, at the annuity rates applicable at that time. The Trap: Higher returns (Option B) depends on market conditions, not the timing of income start. Payment frequency (Option C) is a payout-option choice, not the defining difference between immediate and deferred annuities. Note: The defining distinction is when annuity payments begin. In a deferred annuity, the corpus is built during the deferment period and annuity income starts at the vesting age, using the annuity rates applicable when the annuity is actually bought.
